_readme: Draft of the MgT2E trade rules, filled only from assets/trade.txt (Johnny's extracted text of the Trade chapter) by stream Z on 2026-10-17. Every row carries _src: the line or lines of assets/trade.txt it came from. Nothing was taken from memory and nothing inferred; a cell the text does not settle is null. Johnny answered the ZT0 questions on 2026-10-17 (directives/streams/Z.md, ZT0b); a row his answer settles carries _answer, and every null left says why in _answer.

Shape: the skeleton's keys, with these changes. goods became an object: goods.table is the Trade Goods table (one entry per D66 row) and goods.availability holds the rules for what a supplier has. fares is new: the Passage and Freight table, one row per parsec, read by passengers and freight. localBrokers is the skeleton's broker, named as the text names it. illegalGoods is new (the ILLEGAL GOODS box). tradeRoutes is dropped (Johnny, ZT0 Q11): the text has no trade routes table.

Rows rebuilt from wrapped extraction cite every line used. Where a Trade Goods row has its Purchase DM and Sale DM columns on one line with no comma between them (for example line 563, 'Asteroid +4 Industrial +3, Non-'), the column break is taken at the missing comma: entries inside one column are comma-separated in every row of the table (question 2).

Values: credits are numbers in Cr (MCr1 is 1000000); dice stay as printed ('2D x 10', '1D'); percentages are numbers; DM keys and availability are the printed words, line wraps joined, spelling untouched (Johnny, ZT0 Q3: names stay as printed; a name-to-trade-code table goes in the trade module later).

Also settled by Johnny on 2026-10-17: four passages (high, middle, basic, low), as line 44's list has (Q1); the Population-code goods sentence split across lines 352 and 395 is one sentence (Q6); selling is 3D (Q9).
The Random Passenger table (lines 213-236) is already in findings/rules_drafts/mgt2e_random_passenger.json and is not repeated here.
Moves to rules/mgt2e_trade.json only on Johnny's word (CLAUDE.md rule 1), then npm run rules:gen.

Mail containers take up five tons of space and the Travellers will be paid Cr25000 for transporting the container. notes.text: The size of the Starport provides a bonus to finding a supplier.
A Traveller must find a buyer, instead of a supplier. The same rules apply.

rules.text: Common Goods can be purchased on any world. Trade Goods can usually only be found on a world with a matching Trade code.
The tons column on the Trade Goods table determines how many tons of a given type of goods are available for purchase.

rules.label: On Population 3- apply DM-3 to the roll for quantity
Population 9+ worlds have vast economies and grant DM+3 on the roll for lot quantities

rules.text: A supplier will have all Common Goods available, the Trade Goods that match the world's Trade codes and a quantity of randomly determined goods equal to the Population code of the world.

Roll on the Trade Goods table to randomly determine the goods available, re-rolling results 61-65 unless dealing with a black market supplier. If you roll the same type of goods multiple times, then the supplier has extra amounts of those goods available.
A black market supplier has whatever illegal goods match world's Trade codes, as well as any randomly rolled illegal goods. Roll 1D on the Trade Goods table and use 6 as the leading digit.

kinds.name: Local broker or fixer
kinds._note: possibly higher for highly illegal or dangerous cargos

notes.text: If the roll to determine the fixer's skill is a natural 2, they are an informer, government agent or double-crosser. The referee should determine resulting events.
Some goods are illegal throughout the Imperium. These are marked as illegal in the Trade Goods tables. Other goods are illegal only on particular worlds (see Law Level, page 255).
Universally illegal goods have high Sale DMs. For other banned goods, their Sale DM is the difference between the Law Level they are banned at and the Law Level of the world.

Military Weapons are banned at Law Level 3. If a trader smuggles any weapons onto a Law Level 9 world, the weapons have Sale DM+6 (if a type of goods is both universally and locally illegal, use whichever Sale DM is higher).
If the trader is caught, they face fines or imprisonment. See Law Levels, page 255.
